newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus opposition leaders face trial - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition leaders face trial - Interfax.

text.p: Two leading opponents of Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, both of them senior members of a previous parliament, will appear in court on Thursday over their role in protest rallies last weekend, Interfax news agency said.

It quoted Mecheslav Grib, a former parliamentary speaker, as saying he and a former first deputy speaker, Vasily Novikov, were accused of breaching public order and the law over a rally and unauthorised march in the capital Minsk to mark the former Soviet republic's Constitution Day on March 15.

Interfax, in a report from Minsk, quoted a source in the state prosecutor's office saying criminal proceedings had been instituted against them for "insulting the state flag" and "incitement to overthrow the current constitutional order" during demonstrations last Friday and Saturday.
Lukashenko scrapped the old parliament in November after winning a referendum which gave him vastly expanded powers. He replaced it with an assembly more favourable to himself.

A strong advocate of re-uniting with Moscow, Lukashenko has broad support among the population of 10 million but faces vocal opposition from a variety of groups, many of which want to preserve their recently acquired independence from Russia.

The president has ordered strict controls on political meetings and the display of nationalist symbols. Police beat and arrested dozens of protesters last weekend and detained a number of opposition leaders.
